title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (2027-02-10)
author: Maya Henderson
content:
Summary:
This combined product document captures the current product overview, the high-level PRD and requirements, key design specs, roadmap and strategic themes for Unified Inference, pricing and packaging recommendations, and consolidated release notes for the most recent increments. It is intended to serve as the canonical reference for product, engineering, go-to-market, and sales when planning feature rollouts, commercial packaging, and customer enablement.

1) Product overview
Purpose and positioning:
- Unified Inference is Redwood's umbrella product that unifies Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments under one consistent developer experience and operational model.
- Positioning: developer-first inference platform for production-grade latency, cost-efficiency, and deployment flexibility.

Core pillars (user value):
- Predictable performance: per-route SLOs (p95 latency targets) and capacity reservation for Dedicated customers.
- Cost-aware controls: batching, caching, quantization profiles, and model routing policies that give customers levers to control unit economics.
- Unified API & UX: same API surface, SDKs, and console for hosted, dedicated and private modes.

Primary personas:
- ML Engineers: model rollouts, evals, and performance tuning
- Backend Engineers: latency & cost constraints, integration, retries/fallbacks
- Platform Teams: standardized inference across business units, compliance/observability needs

2) PRD: Goals, scope, and success metrics
Goals (next 12 months):
1. Complete GA for Unified Inference v2: feature parity across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private for model rollouts, automatic fallback, and route-level SLOs.
2. Reduce average per-token cost for standard text-generation workloads by 20% through batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize.
3. Deliver a pricing & packaging refresh that simplifies tiering and increases upsell conversion for Dedicated customers by 15%.

Problem statements:
- Customers struggle to get consistent latency across deployment modes; model variants and hardware heterogeneity create regressions during rollouts.
- Pricing complexity for Dedicated customers creates friction at procurement/PO stage and lengthens sales cycles.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
- In-scope: route-level SLO config and enforcement, canary and A/B rollouts with traffic-split and automatic fallback, Redwood Optimize recommendations surfaced in Console, a new Dedicated packaging tier and renewal workflow.
- Out-of-scope: full-service managed model retraining, custom hardware development.

Key success metrics (OKRs):
- SLO attainment: 99.5% p95 latency SLO attainment for Hosted tier; 99.9% for Dedicated customers (measured monthly).
- Cost: 20% reduction in median cost-per-1k-tokens for target workloads within 9 months of rollout.
- Commercial: 15% increase in Dedicated upsell conversion and 10% higher average contract value (ACV) in next 12 months.

3) Requirements (functional & non-functional)
Functional requirements:
- FR-001: API compatibility - same endpoints & SDK contracts for text-generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking across deployment modes.
- FR-002: Rollouts - support canary (traffic %), A/B testing (split by user id), and automatic fallback to a compatible variant or region when SLOs are at risk.
- FR-003: Console - show per-route token breakdown, model variant performance heatmaps, and Optimize-suggested configs.
- FR-004: Quantization profiles - provide at least three validated quantization profiles per model family with recommended accuracy vs. cost tradeoffs.

Non-functional requirements (NFRs):
- NFR-001: Latency SLOs - p95 <= 120ms for short text generation (<= 128 tokens) in Hosted region-forward requests.
- NFR-002: Reliability - platform must provide failover to alternate region within 2s for cross-region read requests.
- NFR-003: Security - audit logs for model access, KMS integration for Private deployments, and role-based access controls for rollout operations.

Requirements matrix (example):
| ID | Requirement | Priority | Owner |
| FR-001 | API compatibility | P0 | eng-developer-experience |
| FR-002 | Rollouts (canary, A/B, fallback) | P0 | eng-platform |
| FR-003 | Console visibility & Optimize suggestions | P1 | product-engineering |
| FR-004 | Quantization profiles | P1 | eng-serving-runtime |

4) Design specs (high-level)
Architecture overview:
- Control plane (Redwood Control): central orchestration for rollouts, policy engine, and billing. Responsible for storing config and coordinating cross-region rollouts.
- Data plane (Serving runtime): optimized, GPU-backed inference with kernel selection, KV cache, and batching. Exposes local admission controller for latency-aware batching.
- Routing & Fallback service: policy-driven router that can route by latency, cost, region, or customer tier. Integrates with runtime health metrics for automatic fallback.

Key components and interfaces:
- Rollout Manager API: POST /rollouts -> {route_id, model_variant, strategy, traffic_split, evaluation_criteria}
- SLO Policy Engine: declarative policy language used by Rollout Manager to decide rollback or fallback triggers. Example rule: "if p95 > 1.2 * baseline_p95 for 5m then fallback to variant X".

Data models and constraints:
- ModelVariant metadata (string labels): model_id, quantization_profile, kernel_profile, compat_regions (list of region codes).
- Sticky routing: per-user sticky sessions for chat use-cases must honor KV cache locality.

Design tradeoffs considered:
- Centralized vs. decentralized rollout decisioning: chose centralized control plane to ensure consistent cross-region rollouts and clear audit trails at the expense of slightly higher control-plane latency.
- Conservative fallback thresholds to prioritize reliability over speculative performance optimizations.

CLI examples (developer workflows):
- Create a canary rollout (example):
  redwood rollout create --route payments-summary --variant model-v2-q8 --strategy canary --traffic 5 --evaluate-metrics p95,accuracy --auto-fallback true

5) Roadmap & themes (next four quarters)
Themes by quarter:
- Q1: Stabilize rollouts & SLO enforcement (complete SLO policy engine, rollout audit trail, canary ergonomics)
- Q2: Cost optimization push (Improve batching heuristics, KV cache persistence, rollout of quantization profiles)
- Q3: Enterprise packaging & compliance (Private GA, Dedicated expanded pricing tiers, KMS/HSM deep integrations)
- Q4: Observability & quality (evals-driven regressions, per-prompt quality alerts, trace-level latency attribution)

Planned milestones (dates are target delivery):
- 2027-02-15: Rollout Manager API v1 (canary & basic fallback) - Beta
- 2027-04-30: SLO Policy Engine v1 and Console SLO dashboards - GA
- 2027-06-15: Redwood Optimize Quantization Profiles v1 - GA
- 2027-09-01: Dedicated Tier: Enterprise Plus + Renewal workflow - GA

Dependencies and risks:
- Dependency: eng-serving-runtime kernel support for quantized kernels (blocking for quantization rollouts).
- Risk: aggressive batching could increase tail latency for small interactive workloads; mitigated by latency-aware admission control.

6) Pricing & packaging notes
Pricing goals:
- Simpler tiers that map to buyer intents: Developer (self-serve Hosted), Scale (committed Dedicated), and Enterprise (Private + Compliance add-ons).
- Provide predictable Dedicated pricing with optional burst capacity.

Proposed tier matrix (high level):
| Tier | Billing model | Key features |
| Developer | usage-based (per-token + per-embedding) | Hosted API, basic console, community support |
| Scale | reserved capacity (monthly commit) + overage | Dedicated GPU pools, SLA, burst options, 30d retention |
| Enterprise | annual license + platform fee | Private deployment, KMS/HSM, SOC2/ISO attestations, enhanced SLAs |

Dedicated pricing packaging changes (recommended):
- Introduce a Standard and Plus dedicated tier. Standard: baseline GPU pool with autoscaling policies. Plus: guaranteed headroom, priority routing, and SRE-backed runbook with 24/7 escalation.
- Renewal workflow: simplify upgrade path with 30/60-day notifications and an online amendment flow for committed capacity.

Commercial playbook notes for sales:
1. Use Developer tier to drive adoption; target conversion to Scale after >$10k monthly spend via pilot discounts.
2. For Enterprise deals emphasize Private's compliance controls and integration support; offer Professional Services for on-prem pack.

7) Release notes (consolidated for recent increments)
Release 2027-02-10 (v2.1):
- GA: Rollout Manager API v1 (canary + basic auto-fallback).
- Beta: SLO dashboards (console) and per-route token cost breakdown.
- Improvements: 10-15% average token cost reduction for selected workloads via improved batching heuristics.
- Known issues: Quantization profiles available for a subset of models; accuracy regressions observed for model-family X at q6 profiles (tracking in eng-serving-runtime/known-issues).

Release 2026-12-01 (v2.0):
- Major: Unified API parity across Hosted & Dedicated for text generation and embeddings.
- Added: Traffic-split API and rollout audit trail entries in Control plane logs.
- Fixed: SDK timeout mismatch causing increased p95 on SDK v1.4 clients.

Rollback & incident playbook (summary):
1. Identify: alert from SLO engine or ops reporting increased p95/5xx for route.
2. Evaluate: check Rollout Manager history and recent rollouts; evaluate canary metrics vs baseline for 10m-window.
3. Action: perform immediate rollback via CLI: redwood rollout rollback --route payments-summary --to-previous true OR trigger auto-fallback to variant X via control plane.
4. Postmortem: create incident in oncall-and-incident-response with tags: service:control-plane, severity, and publish to stakeholders within 48h.

8) Ownership & next steps
Owners:
- Product: Maya Henderson (overall product & roadmap)
- Engineering: Priya Nair (platform & rollouts), Diego Morales (serving runtime), Liam O'Connor (Optimize & cost tooling)

Immediate next steps (next 30 days):
1. Finalize SLO policy rules and map to console UI fields (owner: Priya).
2. Complete canary evaluation metrics contract and expose in Rollout Manager API (owner: Diego).
3. Publish Dedicated tier pricing sheet and update sales playbook (owner: Liam).
